cards.cardText: The City Inside, a rabbit cross-section revealing an industrial cityscape. It has been running the civilization while you were busy.
The Citizen, a hydra of animals erupting from the neck. You never once told this city what to do; it never once asked your permission.
The Heart, a badger on a massive drum kit. The brain can modify the rate; the brain cannot generate it. The badger drums alone.
The Lungs, two giant broccoli trees exchanging blue and red birds: seventy square meters folded into your chest, the only manual override.
The Gut, zombie commuters boarding: eighty percent of the phone calls go up to the brain. The subway runs the city.
The Night Shift, mice in janitor overalls cleaning inside a glowing skull. Sleep is the janitorial shift washing the thoughts out of the carpet.
The Immune System, armored rats with riot shields spotlighting a virus. A library of every murder attempt. It remembers things you have forgotten.
Inflammation, a fire salamander with a flamethrower: the response that heals the wound becomes the mechanism that burns the city.
Autoimmune, a crazed dog biting itself: the discrimination fails, not the weapon. The gun works fine; it's just pointed the wrong way.
DNA Replication, a black spider weaving a double helix web: one error per billion letters. You have had cancer many times; the spider usually eats it.
Cancer, a giant crab with a fortress built on its shell. Evolution occurring inside you. It is not a disease; it is a competitor.
The Aging Thymus, an old elephant in a crumbling library. Your immune repertoire was built when you were a teenager. Hope you read good books.
Andreas Vesalius, a mole in an Elizabethan ruff stomping on a Galen textbook: he looked at the body instead of the book. Everyone else was wrong.
Ignaz Semmelweis, a raccoon washing his hands in a lime bucket while silhouettes mock: he saved the mothers. The doctors committed him.
The Semmelweis Problem, a barn door bursting open with rays of light: the evidence is available, the implication is uncomfortable, we reject the finding.
The Humoralist, a tortoise carrying four potion bottles, one spilling: wrong in the facts, right in the vibe. It was the first Kayfabe.
The Blind Eye: you have a hole in your vision. The brain fills it in with best guesses. Trust, but verify.
The Brain, five owls in judge wigs arguing over a burning map: the decision was already underway five hundred milliseconds before you made it. You are the press secretary, not the president.
The Scorekeeper, a sea urchin writing with a feather quill in a leather-bound ledger: the body keeps the score because the body is the score.
